hypotheses.text: Recessive NOTCH3-associated arteriopathy exhibits a strict genotype-phenotype divergence: biallelic loss-of-function (null/cysteine-sparing) variants present in infancy or early childhood (typically under 2 years of age) with developmental delay, seizures, spasticity, and childhood strokes, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants present in early adulthood (3rd to 5th decades) with classic CADASIL-spectrum lacunar strokes and progressive subcortical dementia.
hypotheses.rationale: Resolves the contradiction on age of onset and clinical presentation in biallelic NOTCH3 cases by stratifying patients by variant mechanism (loss-of-function vs cysteine-involving missense), explaining why some cohorts report adult-onset CADASIL phenocopies while others report infantile neurodevelopmental leukodystrophies.

evidence.text: Systematic analysis of 50 patients with biallelic NOTCH3 variants verified that biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with spasticity and childhood-onset stroke, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within the CADASIL spectrum with early adulthood-onset stroke and dementia.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

evidence.text: Three patients from two families with bi-allelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants presented at 9 to 14 months of age with developmental delay and seizures, followed by cognitive impairment and variably recurrent strokes.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: The patients presented at 9 to 14 months of age with developmental delay, seizures, or both. The disease course was characterized by cognitive impairment and variably recurrent strokes, migraine attacks, and seizures.

evidence.text: Two siblings with homozygous null nonsense variants (p.Arg735Ter) presented with severe congenital manifestations including eye misalignment, visual impairment, epilepsy, global developmental delay, and pyramidal signs.

source.title: Autosomal recessive NOTCH3-related leukodystrophy in two siblings and review of the literature
source.quote: These patients presented with a severe congenital phenotype, including eye misalignment, visual impairment, epilepsy, global developmental delay, and subsequent development of pyramidal signs. Biallelic nonsense variants were discovered in both the cases (NM_000435.3:c.2203 C > T (p. [Arg735Ter]).

hypotheses.text: Sparing of the anterior temporal pole white matter hyperintensities on brain MRI is a distinctive negative radiological hallmark of biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function leukoencephalopathy, discriminating it from both classic dominant CADASIL and biallelic cysteine-involving NOTCH3 arteriopathy.
hypotheses.rationale: Neuroimaging involvement of the anterior temporal lobes is considered a hallmark for CADASIL; demonstrating consistent absence/sparing in biallelic loss-of-function NOTCH3 cases provides an objective neuroradiological rule-out marker.

evidence.text: In three pediatric patients with bi-allelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants with extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, lacunes, and calcifications, the anterior temporal lobes were explicitly spared.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: MRI findings pointed at a small vessel disease, with extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, atrophy, lacunes in the basal ganglia, microbleeds, and microcalcifications. The anterior temporal lobes were spared.

evidence.text: A proband with a novel homozygous NOTCH3 null variant presented with ataxia, livedo racemosa, cognitive decline, seizures, and white matter abnormalities with confirmed absence of anterior temporal pole lesions.

source.title: Distinct neurological phenotypes associated with biallelic loss of NOTCH3 function: evidence for recessive inheritance
source.quote: Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed on a proband who exhibited livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and MRI white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions.

hypotheses.text: Brain MRI in biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function arteriopathy is characterized by periatrial white matter volume loss mimicking periventricular leukomalacia (PVL), whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense cases present with deep white matter hyperintensities without marked volume loss.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifies the neuroradiological dichotomy between loss-of-function and missense mechanisms, allowing clinicians to distinguish recessive leukodystrophy from congenital/perinatal hypoxic-ischemic injury (PVL) or classic CADASIL.

evidence.text: Neuroradiological evaluation showed that biallelic loss-of-function variants lead to periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia, unlike biallelic cysteine missense variants which show deep white matter lesions without volume loss.

Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

hypotheses.text: Heterozygous carrier relatives of patients with recessive biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function variants do not develop premature ischemic strokes or early vascular dementia, demonstrating a lack of dominant CADASIL-like pathogenicity.
hypotheses.rationale: Essential for pedigree interpretation and family counselling: distinguishes benign or subclinical monoallelic loss-of-function status from dominant CADASIL alleles that cause recurrent strokes in heterozygotes.

evidence.text: Systematic cohort review showed that monoallelic carriers of NOTCH3 loss-of-function variants remain predominantly asymptomatic, with only occasional non-specific headaches reported.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Notably, monoallelic carriers of loss-of-function variants are predominantly asymptomatic, with only a few cases reporting nonspecific headaches.

evidence.text: Pedigree analysis of a homozygous NOTCH3 null variant proband confirmed that consanguineous heterozygous parents were healthy, and incidental heterozygous null variants in unrelated individuals did not produce CADASIL manifestations.

source.title: Distinct neurological phenotypes associated with biallelic loss of NOTCH3 function: evidence for recessive inheritance
source.quote: The consanguineous parents were confirmed as heterozygous variant carriers. In addition, three heterozygous NOTCH3 null variants were reported as incidental findings in three unrelated cases analyzed in our center.

numbers.metric: incidental heterozygous null cases without CADASIL

evidence.text: In a family study, relatives carrying the frameshift loss-of-function variant p.Cys1024Valfs248 alone exhibited a mild imaging phenotype without increased stroke risk or vascular NOTCH3 extracellular domain immunoreactivity.

source.title: An in trans NOTCH3 loss-of-function variant modifies disease severity in CADASIL: A family-based study
source.quote: In contrast, the father (carrying p.Cys1146Ser alone) and the mother and brother (carrying p.Cys1024Valfs248 alone) exhibited milder clinical and imaging phenotypes. Only the carriers of the cysteine-altering variant demonstrated NOTCH3 extracellular domain (NOTCH3 ECD ) immunoreactivity in skin vessels.

new_directions.question_text: What is the precise prevalence of livedo racemosa and systemic vascular signs in biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function patients compared to Sneddon syndrome or CARASIL?
new_directions.rationale: Livedo racemosa was documented in Tasharrofi et al. and referenced in Al et al., but absent in others; determining its penetrance will establish whether cutaneous livedo serves as a discriminating diagnostic clue for recessive NOTCH3 SVD.

new_directions.question_text: Does compound heterozygosity of one cysteine-altering missense variant and one loss-of-function variant in trans exacerbate CADASIL stroke severity and accelerate age of onset compared to classical monoallelic CADASIL?
new_directions.rationale: Lan et al. (2026) described severe early-onset progression in a trans-compound heterozygote, suggesting NOTCH3 haploinsufficiency combined with neomorphic cysteine toxicity may produce an intermediate, aggravated clinical trajectory.
